review.reason: Candidate 17 passes as supplied. Hole 1 is a 209-yard par 3 played with a 3-wood. Its water on the right and bunkers around the target make line and distance matter, while the playable tee dispersion leaves room for a recoverable miss. Hole 2 is a 330-yard split-fairway par 4: the separated landing routes create a positional choice, and its tighter safe-shot results make placement consequential. Hole 3 is a 560-yard three-shot par 5 with fairway bunkers and a broad staged route, providing a substantial long-game finish rather than another short target hole. The par-3/4/5 sequence, different tee demands, and contrasting target, split-route, and staged-play strategies create strong variety within the round. Recent courses include similar par and hole-type combinations, but this set stands apart with its split-fairway middle hole and water limited to the opener. The shot-to-green simulations and tee-dispersion probes support a challenging round with playable routes, not three routine scoring opportunities or an exact-shot trap.
